question: What's the average score of a question?
reference_sql: select avg(score) from posts_questions
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: what is the highest view count any question has reached
reference_sql: select max(view_count) from posts_questions
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many different tags are actually in use on questions?
reference_sql: select count(distinct tag_id) from post_tags
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many answers were marked as the accepted one?
reference_sql: select count(*) from posts_answers where is_accepted=1
alt_sqls: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts_questions WHERE accepted_answer_id IS NOT NULL
notes: By the answer flag (70,896); counting questions that point to an accepted answer (71,353) is accepted too.

question: On average, how many tags does a question have?
reference_sql: select cast((select count(*) from post_tags) as real)/(select count(*) from posts_questions)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: number of users with more than 10000 reputation
reference_sql: select count(*) from users where reputation>10000
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many comments sit on questions compared with comments on answers?
reference_sql: select (select count(*) from comments c where c.post_id in (select post_id from posts_questions)) as on_questions, (select count(*) from comments c where c.post_id in (select post_id from posts_answers)) as on_answers
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: What is the average number of badges per user?
reference_sql: select avg(badge_count) from users
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: total views of all python questions
reference_sql: select sum(q.view_count) from posts_questions q where q.post_id in (select pt.post_id from post_tags pt join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id where t.tag_name='python')
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: top 10 tags by number of questions
reference_sql: select t.tag_name,count(*) n from post_tags pt join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id group by t.tag_id order by n desc limit 10
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Who wrote the most answers? Give me the top 10 names and their answer counts.
reference_sql: select u.display_name,count(*) n from posts_answers a join users u on u.user_id=a.user_id group by u.user_id order by n desc limit 10
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Who asked the 10 most viewed questions?
reference_sql: select u.display_name,q.title,q.view_count from posts_questions q join users u on u.user_id=q.user_id order by q.view_count desc limit 10
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Compare the average question score for python, java and javascript.
reference_sql: select t.tag_name,avg(q.score) avg_score,count(*) n from posts_questions q join post_tags pt on pt.post_id=q.post_id join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id where t.tag_name in ('python','java','javascript') group by t.tag_name
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Which tags most often show up alongside python?
reference_sql: select t.tag_name,count(*) n from post_tags p1 join tags t1 on t1.tag_id=p1.tag_id and t1.tag_name='python' join post_tags pt on pt.post_id=p1.post_id join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id where t.tag_name<>'python' group by t.tag_id order by n desc limit 10
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Which users have both a reputation above 5000 and more than 50 answers written in this data? List them with their numbers.
reference_sql: SELECT "display_name", "reputation", "answers" FROM (select u.user_id,u.display_name,u.reputation,count(*) answers from users u join posts_answers a on a.user_id=u.user_id where u.reputation>5000 group by u.user_id having count(*)>50 order by answers desc)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Which questions have the most comments directly on them? Show the titles.
reference_sql: SELECT "title", "n" FROM (with c as (select post_id,count(*) n from comments where post_id in (select post_id from posts_questions) group by post_id) select q.post_id,q.title,c.n from c join posts_questions q on q.post_id=c.post_id where c.n=(select max(n) from c))
alt_sqls: SELECT "post_id", "n" FROM (with c as (select post_id,count(*) n from comments where post_id in (select post_id from posts_questions) group by post_id) select q.post_id,q.title,c.n from c join posts_questions q on q.post_id=c.post_id where c.n=(select max(n) from c))
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many docker questions got an accepted answer?
reference_sql: select count(*) from posts_questions q where q.accepted_answer_id is not null and q.post_id in (select pt.post_id from post_tags pt join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id where t.tag_name='docker')
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Who answers their own questions the most?
reference_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT a.user_id, COUNT(*) n FROM posts_answers a JOIN posts_questions q ON q.post_id = a.parent_id AND q.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY a.user_id) SELECT u.display_name FROM s JOIN users u ON u.user_id = s.user_id WHERE s.n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM s)
notes: 'The most' returns one row; a tie would return all tied users (there is none: 8 against 6).

question: Is the average reputation of people asking rust questions different from those asking go questions?
reference_sql: select t.tag_name,avg(u.reputation) avg_rep,count(*) n from posts_questions q join users u on u.user_id=q.user_id join post_tags pt on pt.post_id=q.post_id join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id where t.tag_name in ('rust','go') group by t.tag_name
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Top 10 people answering kubernetes questions
reference_sql: SELECT u.display_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM posts_answers a JOIN users u ON u.user_id = a.user_id WHERE a.parent_id IN (SELECT pt.post_id FROM post_tags pt JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = pt.tag_id WHERE t.tag_name = 'kubernetes') GROUP BY u.user_id ORDER BY n DESC, u.display_name LIMIT 10
notes: Rows that tie on the count may come in any order.

question: Which answer has the highest score, who wrote it and what was the question about?
reference_sql: SELECT "score", "display_name", "title" FROM (select a.post_id,a.score,u.display_name,q.title from posts_answers a join users u on u.user_id=a.user_id join posts_questions q on q.post_id=a.parent_id order by a.score desc limit 1)
alt_sqls: SELECT "post_id", "score", "display_name" FROM (select a.post_id,a.score,u.display_name,q.title from posts_answers a join users u on u.user_id=a.user_id join posts_questions q on q.post_id=a.parent_id order by a.score desc limit 1)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: For the 5 tags with the most answers, how many answers does each have?
reference_sql: select t.tag_name,count(*) answers from posts_answers a join post_tags pt on pt.post_id=a.parent_id join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id group by t.tag_id order by answers desc limit 5
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Among tags with at least 100 questions, which ones have the highest average views per question?
reference_sql: select t.tag_name,count(*) questions,avg(q.view_count) avg_views from posts_questions q join post_tags pt on pt.post_id=q.post_id join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id group by t.tag_id having count(*)>=100 order by avg_views desc limit 10
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many people have commented on a question that they asked themselves?
reference_sql: select count(distinct c.user_id) from comments c join posts_questions q on q.post_id=c.post_id and q.user_id=c.user_id
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: List users who joined in 2021 and have already written more than 10 answers, with their names and answer counts.
reference_sql: SELECT "display_name", "n" FROM (select u.user_id,u.display_name,count(*) n from users u join posts_answers a on a.user_id=u.user_id where u.creation_date>='2021-01-01' and u.creation_date<'2022-01-01' group by u.user_id having count(*)>10 order by n desc)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: What are the 3 most common tags on questions that scored 50 or more?
reference_sql: SELECT t.tag_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM posts_questions q JOIN post_tags pt ON pt.post_id = q.post_id JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = pt.tag_id WHERE q.score >= 50 GROUP BY t.tag_id ORDER BY n DESC, t.tag_name LIMIT 3
notes: Changed from top 10 to top 3 because the counts tie at 10th place; reactjs and javascript tie at 8 and may swap.

question: Which askers have collected the most total views across all their questions?
reference_sql: select u.display_name,sum(q.view_count) v from posts_questions q join users u on u.user_id=q.user_id group by u.user_id order by v desc limit 10
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: List questions with 'memory leak' in the title and the names of the people who asked them.
reference_sql: SELECT "title", "display_name" FROM (select q.post_id,q.title,u.display_name from posts_questions q join users u on u.user_id=q.user_id where lower(q.title) like '%memory leak%')
alt_sqls: SELECT "post_id", "display_name" FROM (select q.post_id,q.title,u.display_name from posts_questions q join users u on u.user_id=q.user_id where lower(q.title) like '%memory leak%')
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many upvotes did the questions tagged python get compared with the ones tagged java?
reference_sql: select t.tag_name,count(*) upvotes from votes v join post_tags pt on pt.post_id=v.post_id join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id where v.vote_type='UpMod' and t.tag_name in ('python','java') and v.post_id in (select post_id from posts_questions) group by t.tag_name
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many questions never got a single answer?
reference_sql: select count(*) from posts_questions q where not exists (select 1 from posts_answers a where a.parent_id=q.post_id)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many users only ever wrote comments and never posted a question or an answer?
reference_sql: select count(*) from users u where exists (select 1 from comments c where c.user_id=u.user_id) and not exists (select 1 from posts_questions q where q.user_id=u.user_id) and not exists (select 1 from posts_answers a where a.user_id=u.user_id)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: how many tags exist that are not used by any question
reference_sql: select count(*) from tags t where not exists (select 1 from post_tags p where p.tag_id=t.tag_id)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many answers have never received any vote?
reference_sql: select count(*) from posts_answers a where not exists (select 1 from votes v where v.post_id=a.post_id)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Number of questions that got answers but none of them was accepted
reference_sql: select count(*) from posts_questions q where exists (select 1 from posts_answers a where a.parent_id=q.post_id) and not exists (select 1 from posts_answers a where a.parent_id=q.post_id and a.is_accepted=1)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Of the people who signed up in 2021, how many have never asked a question?
reference_sql: select count(*) from users u where u.creation_date>='2021-01-01' and u.creation_date<'2022-01-01' and not exists (select 1 from posts_questions q where q.user_id=u.user_id)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Which users have written the most answers without ever having a single one accepted? Show the top 8.
reference_sql: SELECT u.display_name, COUNT(*) AS answers FROM posts_answers a JOIN users u ON u.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id HAVING SUM(a.is_accepted) = 0 ORDER BY answers DESC, u.display_name LIMIT 8
notes: Changed from top 10 to top 8: the counts tie at 9 across places 9 to 11, but place 8 (10 answers) is clear.

question: How many questions never received an upvote?
reference_sql: select count(*) from posts_questions q where not exists (select 1 from votes v where v.post_id=q.post_id and v.vote_type='UpMod')
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: top tags 2021
reference_sql: select t.tag_name,count(*) n from posts_questions q join post_tags pt on pt.post_id=q.post_id join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id where q.creation_date>='2021-01-01' and q.creation_date<'2022-01-01' group by t.tag_id order by n desc limit 10
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many questions were asked in the last 6 months?
reference_sql: select count(*) from posts_questions where creation_date>='2022-03-25'
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: At what hour of the day are the most answers posted?
reference_sql: SELECT CAST(substr(creation_date, 12, 2) AS INT) AS hour_utc, COUNT(*) AS n FROM posts_answers GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1
alt_sqls: SELECT substr(creation_date, 12, 2) AS hour_utc, COUNT(*) AS n FROM posts_answers GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1
notes: UTC hour. The alternate gives the hour as text ('14') instead of a number.

question: How many new accounts were created each year?
reference_sql: select substr(creation_date,1,4) yr,count(*) from users group by yr order by yr
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: On average, how many hours pass between a question being asked and its first answer?
reference_sql: select avg((julianday(f.first_a)-julianday(q.creation_date))*24) from posts_questions q join (select parent_id,min(creation_date) first_a from posts_answers group by parent_id) f on f.parent_id=q.post_id
alt_sqls: SELECT AVG(julianday(fa.first_a) - julianday(q.creation_date)) FROM posts_questions q JOIN (SELECT parent_id, MIN(creation_date) first_a FROM posts_answers GROUP BY parent_id) fa ON fa.parent_id = q.post_id
notes: Mean hours from question to first answer, over answered questions. Days are accepted too.

question: Which month had the most questions ever?
reference_sql: select substr(creation_date,1,7) m,count(*) n from posts_questions group by m order by n desc limit 1
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: how many questions this year so far
reference_sql: select count(*) from posts_questions where creation_date>='2022-01-01'
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Which tags got the most new questions in the last 3 months of the data?
reference_sql: select t.tag_name,count(*) n from posts_questions q join post_tags pt on pt.post_id=q.post_id join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id where q.creation_date>='2022-06-25' group by t.tag_id order by n desc limit 10
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many questions received their first answer on the same calendar day they were asked?
reference_sql: select count(*) from posts_questions q join (select parent_id,min(creation_date) f from posts_answers group by parent_id) x on x.parent_id=q.post_id where substr(x.f,1,10)=substr(q.creation_date,1,10)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How many comments were written in each month of 2022?
reference_sql: select substr(creation_date,1,7) m,count(*) from comments where creation_date>='2022-01-01' and creation_date<'2023-01-01' group by m order by m
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Did more questions get asked in the first quarter of 2021 or the first quarter of 2022, and by how much?
reference_sql: select sum(creation_date>='2021-01-01' and creation_date<'2021-04-01') q1_2021,sum(creation_date>='2022-01-01' and creation_date<'2022-04-01') q1_2022,sum(creation_date>='2022-01-01' and creation_date<'2022-04-01')-sum(creation_date>='2021-01-01' and creation_date<'2021-04-01') diff from posts_questions
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Which people who registered before 2012 are still answering questions in 2022? Show the top few by number of answers this year.
reference_sql: SELECT u.display_name, COUNT(*) AS answers_2022 FROM posts_answers a JOIN users u ON u.user_id = a.user_id WHERE u.creation_date < '2012-01-01' AND substr(a.creation_date, 1, 4) = '2022' GROUP BY a.user_id ORDER BY answers_2022 DESC, a.user_id LIMIT 5
notes: 'Top few' is read as 5.

question: How many questions were posted on weekends versus on weekdays?
reference_sql: select case when cast(strftime('%w',creation_date) as int) in (0,6) then 'weekend' else 'weekday' end k,count(*) from posts_questions group by k
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: What percentage of questions have an accepted answer?
reference_sql: select 100.0*sum(accepted_answer_id is not null)/count(*) from posts_questions
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: What fraction of all questions are tagged with python?
reference_sql: select 1.0*(select count(*) from posts_questions where post_id in (select pt.post_id from post_tags pt join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id where t.tag_name='python'))/(select count(*) from posts_questions)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: For the 10 biggest tags, what share of their questions got an accepted answer?
reference_sql: with big as (select t.tag_id,t.tag_name,count(*) n from post_tags pt join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id group by t.tag_id order by n desc limit 10) select b.tag_name,b.n,100.0*sum(q.accepted_answer_id is not null)/b.n pct from big b join post_tags pt on pt.tag_id=b.tag_id join posts_questions q on q.post_id=pt.post_id group by b.tag_id order by b.n desc
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Which tags grew most in question count from 2020 to 2021, and what share of all 2021 questions did each of them make up?
reference_sql: with y as (select pt.tag_id,substr(q.creation_date,1,4) yr,count(*) n from posts_questions q join post_tags pt on pt.post_id=q.post_id where q.creation_date<'2022-01-01' group by 1,2), tot as (select count(*) n from posts_questions where creation_date>='2021-01-01' and creation_date<'2022-01-01') select t.tag_name,y20.n n2020,y21.n n2021,y21.n-y20.n growth,100.0*y21.n/tot.n share_2021 from y y20 join y y21 on y21.tag_id=y20.tag_id and y20.yr='2020' and y21.yr='2021' join tags t on t.tag_id=y20.tag_id,tot order by growth desc limit 10
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: What percentage of answers were posted within an hour of the question?
reference_sql: select 100.0*sum((julianday(a.creation_date)-julianday(q.creation_date))*24<=1)/count(*) from posts_answers a join posts_questions q on q.post_id=a.parent_id
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Among users with at least 20 answers, who has the highest share of accepted answers? top 10 please
reference_sql: select u.display_name,count(*) answers,sum(a.is_accepted) acc,1.0*sum(a.is_accepted)/count(*) share from posts_answers a join users u on u.user_id=a.user_id group by u.user_id having count(*)>=20 order by share desc,answers desc limit 10
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Which proportion of users have asked at least one question?
reference_sql: select 1.0*(select count(distinct user_id) from posts_questions)/(select count(*) from users)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: share of questions with a zero or negative score
reference_sql: select 1.0*sum(score<=0)/count(*) from posts_questions
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: For each year, what proportion of questions got at least one answer?
reference_sql: select substr(creation_date,1,4) yr,count(*) n,1.0*sum(exists(select 1 from posts_answers a where a.parent_id=q.post_id))/count(*) prop from posts_questions q group by yr order by yr
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: What share of all votes does each vote type account for?
reference_sql: select vote_type,count(*) n,100.0*count(*)/(select count(*) from votes) pct from votes group by vote_type order by n desc
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Who are the top 3 answerers within each of the 5 biggest tags?
reference_sql: with big as (select t.tag_id,t.tag_name from post_tags pt join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id group by t.tag_id order by count(*) desc limit 5), c as (select b.tag_name,a.user_id,count(*) n from posts_answers a join post_tags pt on pt.post_id=a.parent_id join big b on b.tag_id=pt.tag_id group by b.tag_id,a.user_id), r as (select *,row_number() over (partition by tag_name order by n desc,user_id) rn from c) select r.tag_name,u.display_name,r.n,r.rn from r join users u on u.user_id=r.user_id where rn<=3 order by tag_name,rn
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Show a running total of questions asked, month by month.
reference_sql: with m as (select substr(creation_date,1,7) m,count(*) n from posts_questions group by m) select m,n,sum(n) over (order by m) running from m order by m
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: For each year, which question had the highest score?
reference_sql: SELECT "yr", "title", "score" FROM (select * from (select substr(q.creation_date,1,4) yr,q.post_id,q.title,q.score,rank() over (partition by substr(q.creation_date,1,4) order by q.score desc) rk from posts_questions q) where rk=1 order by yr)
alt_sqls: SELECT "yr", "post_id", "score" FROM (select * from (select substr(q.creation_date,1,4) yr,q.post_id,q.title,q.score,rank() over (partition by substr(q.creation_date,1,4) order by q.score desc) rk from posts_questions q) where rk=1 order by yr)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Who has the highest reputation among the users who joined in each year since 2018?
reference_sql: SELECT "yr", "display_name", "reputation" FROM (select * from (select substr(creation_date,1,4) yr,user_id,display_name,reputation,rank() over (partition by substr(creation_date,1,4) order by reputation desc) rk from users where creation_date>='2018-01-01') where rk=1 order by yr)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How did the number of questions change from one month to the next in 2021?
reference_sql: select * from (select substr(creation_date,1,7) m,count(*) n,count(*)-lag(count(*)) over (order by substr(creation_date,1,7)) chg from posts_questions group by m) where m>='2021-01' and m<='2021-12' order by m
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: For each of the top 10 tags, what's the most viewed question title?
reference_sql: with big as (select t.tag_id,t.tag_name from post_tags pt join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id group by t.tag_id order by count(*) desc limit 10), r as (select b.tag_name,q.title,q.view_count,row_number() over (partition by b.tag_id order by q.view_count desc) rn from big b join post_tags pt on pt.tag_id=b.tag_id join posts_questions q on q.post_id=pt.post_id) select tag_name,title,view_count from r where rn=1
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: cumulative number of accounts created by year
reference_sql: select substr(creation_date,1,4) yr,count(*) n,sum(count(*)) over (order by substr(creation_date,1,4)) cum from users group by yr order by yr
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: What was the 7-day moving average of daily question counts during August 2022?
reference_sql: with recursive days(d) as (select date('2022-07-25') union all select date(d,'+1 day') from days where d<'2022-08-31'), dc as (select d,(select count(*) from posts_questions where substr(creation_date,1,10)=d) n from days), ma as (select d,avg(n) over (order by d rows between 6 preceding and current row) ma7 from dc) select d,ma7 from ma where d>='2022-08-01'
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: For each month in 2021, which answer got the highest score?
reference_sql: SELECT m AS month, post_id AS answer_id, score FROM (SELECT substr(creation_date, 1, 7) m, post_id, score, rank() OVER (PARTITION BY substr(creation_date, 1, 7) ORDER BY score DESC) rk FROM posts_answers WHERE creation_date >= '2021-01-01' AND creation_date < '2022-01-01') WHERE rk = 1 ORDER BY m, post_id
notes: Month, answer id and score only; ties would give several rows for a month.

question: What's the longest run of consecutive days where at least one question was asked?
reference_sql: with d as (select distinct substr(creation_date,1,10) dt from posts_questions), g as (select dt,julianday(dt)-row_number() over (order by dt) grp from d) select min(dt) start,max(dt) end,count(*) len from g group by grp order by len desc limit 1
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Rank the top 5 tags by questions in each year from 2020 to 2022.
reference_sql: with c as (select substr(q.creation_date,1,4) yr,t.tag_name,count(*) n from posts_questions q join post_tags pt on pt.post_id=q.post_id join tags t on t.tag_id=pt.tag_id group by 1,t.tag_id), r as (select *,row_number() over (partition by yr order by n desc,tag_name) rn from c) select yr,rn,tag_name,n from r where rn<=5 order by yr,rn
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: Put users into reputation quartiles and tell me how many users and the average answer count are in each.
reference_sql: with u as (select u.user_id,u.reputation,ntile(4) over (order by u.reputation) qt,(select count(*) from posts_answers a where a.user_id=u.user_id) ac from users u) select qt,count(*),avg(ac),min(reputation),max(reputation) from u group by qt order by qt
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: who is the most helpful user?
reference_sql: SELECT u.display_name FROM posts_answers a JOIN users u ON u.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY a.user_id HAVING SUM(a.is_accepted) = (SELECT MAX(s) FROM (SELECT SUM(is_accepted) s FROM posts_answers GROUP BY user_id))
notes: 'Helpful' is read as the most accepted answers (591, Gordon Linoff). The user is compared, not the measure.

question: Which questions are the best?
reference_sql: SELECT "title", "score", "view_count" FROM (select post_id,title,score,view_count from posts_questions order by score desc limit 10)
alt_sqls: SELECT "post_id", "score", "view_count" FROM (select post_id,title,score,view_count from posts_questions order by score desc limit 10)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

question: How active was the site in 2021?
reference_sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts_questions WHERE substr(creation_date,1,4)='2021') AS questions, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts_answers WHERE substr(creation_date,1,4)='2021') AS answers, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments WHERE substr(creation_date,1,4)='2021') AS comments, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE substr(creation_date,1,4)='2021') AS new_users
notes: Counts of questions, answers, comments and new accounts in 2021 (the second writer's four columns).

question: Who are the top contributors recently?
reference_sql: SELECT u.display_name FROM (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) n FROM posts_answers WHERE creation_date >= '2022-06-25' GROUP BY user_id UNION ALL SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) FROM posts_questions WHERE creation_date >= '2022-06-25' GROUP BY user_id) x JOIN users u ON u.user_id = x.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id ORDER BY SUM(n) DESC LIMIT 1
notes: Subjective; compared on the top person only (mozway under both writers' readings).

question: Which tag is the hardest?
reference_sql: SELECT t.tag_name FROM posts_questions q JOIN post_tags pt ON pt.post_id = q.post_id JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = pt.tag_id GROUP BY t.tag_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100 ORDER BY 100.0 * SUM(q.accepted_answer_id IS NULL) / COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
notes: Subjective; 'hardest' = highest share of questions without an accepted answer among tags with 100+ questions. Tag name only.

question: Show me the most controversial questions.
reference_sql: SELECT "title", "up", "dn" FROM (with v as (select post_id,sum(vote_type='UpMod') up,sum(vote_type='DownMod') dn from votes group by post_id) select q.post_id,q.title,v.up,v.dn from v join posts_questions q on q.post_id=v.post_id where v.up>0 and v.dn>0 order by min(v.up,v.dn) desc,v.up+v.dn desc limit 10)
alt_sqls: SELECT "post_id", "up", "dn" FROM (with v as (select post_id,sum(vote_type='UpMod') up,sum(vote_type='DownMod') dn from votes group by post_id) select q.post_id,q.title,v.up,v.dn from v join posts_questions q on q.post_id=v.post_id where v.up>0 and v.dn>0 order by min(v.up,v.dn) desc,v.up+v.dn desc limit 10)
notes: Two independent writers derived the same answer.

notes: Unanswerable: votes.user_id is always NULL (voters anonymized).; votes.user_id is NULL for every row (voters anonymized); cannot tell who upvoted.

question: Which user bookmarked the most questions?
notes: Unanswerable: Favorite votes exist but votes.user_id is always NULL, so who bookmarked is unknown.; Favorite votes exist per post but votes.user_id is always NULL, so cannot tell which user bookmarked.

question: How many questions were deleted by moderators?
notes: Unanswerable: no deletion data (deleted posts are not in the data).; No deletion information (deleted posts are absent from the data).

question: Which user wrote the longest comment, and which wrote the shortest?
reference_sql: SELECT u.display_name, length(c.body) AS len FROM comments c JOIN users u ON u.user_id = c.user_id WHERE length(c.body) = (SELECT max(length(body)) FROM comments) UNION ALL SELECT u.display_name, length(c.body) FROM comments c JOIN users u ON u.user_id = c.user_id WHERE length(c.body) = (SELECT min(length(body)) FROM comments)
notes: Two rows: the author of the longest comment (631 characters) and of the shortest (empty).

question: Which user has the longest average comment, among users with at least 10 comments?
reference_sql: SELECT u.display_name FROM comments c JOIN users u ON u.user_id = c.user_id GROUP BY c.user_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10 ORDER BY AVG(length(c.body)) DESC, u.display_name LIMIT 1

question: Which user has the shortest average comment, among users with at least 10 comments?
reference_sql: SELECT u.display_name FROM comments c JOIN users u ON u.user_id = c.user_id GROUP BY c.user_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10 ORDER BY AVG(length(c.body)), u.display_name LIMIT 1

question: Which two users have commented together on the same question the most times? A question counts with all its answers.
reference_sql: WITH cq AS (SELECT DISTINCT qid, user_id FROM (SELECT post_id qid, user_id FROM comments WHERE post_id IN (SELECT post_id FROM posts_questions) UNION ALL SELECT a.parent_id, c.user_id FROM comments c JOIN posts_answers a ON a.post_id = c.post_id)) SELECT ua.display_name AS user_1, ub.display_name AS user_2 FROM cq x JOIN cq y ON x.qid = y.qid AND x.user_id < y.user_id JOIN users ua ON ua.user_id = x.user_id JOIN users ub ON ub.user_id = y.user_id GROUP BY x.user_id, y.user_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, x.user_id, y.user_id LIMIT 1
notes: A question counts together with all its answers. Top pair shares 53 questions (next 51); names may come in either order.

question: How many users have each display-name length? Show the 10 longest lengths.
reference_sql: SELECT length(display_name) AS len, COUNT(*) AS users FROM users GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY len DESC LIMIT 10

question: How many questions have no comments?
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts_questions p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM comments c WHERE c.post_id = p.post_id)
alt_sqls: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts_questions p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM comments c WHERE c.post_id = p.post_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM comments c JOIN posts_answers a ON a.post_id = c.post_id WHERE a.parent_id = p.post_id)
notes: Main reading: no comment directly on the question (64,642). Also accepted: none on the question or any of its answers (37,767).

question: How many answers have no comments?
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts_answers a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM comments c WHERE c.post_id = a.post_id)

question: Which user has the oldest account among those with the least activity, counting their questions, answers and comments?
reference_sql: WITH act AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) n FROM (SELECT user_id FROM posts_questions UNION ALL SELECT user_id FROM posts_answers UNION ALL SELECT user_id FROM comments) GROUP BY user_id) SELECT u.display_name FROM users u LEFT JOIN act a USING (user_id) WHERE coalesce(a.n, 0) = (SELECT min(coalesce(a2.n, 0)) FROM users u2 LEFT JOIN act a2 USING (user_id)) ORDER BY u.creation_date, u.user_id LIMIT 1
notes: Activity = questions + answers + comments. Nobody has none, so the least is one contribution.

question: Which user has the oldest account among those with the least activity, counting only their questions and answers?
reference_sql: WITH act AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) n FROM (SELECT user_id FROM posts_questions UNION ALL SELECT user_id FROM posts_answers) GROUP BY user_id) SELECT u.display_name FROM users u LEFT JOIN act a USING (user_id) WHERE u.user_id <> -1 AND coalesce(a.n, 0) = 0 ORDER BY u.creation_date, u.user_id LIMIT 1
alt_sqls: WITH act AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) n FROM (SELECT user_id FROM posts_questions UNION ALL SELECT user_id FROM posts_answers) GROUP BY user_id) SELECT u.display_name FROM users u LEFT JOIN act a USING (user_id) WHERE coalesce(a.n, 0) = 0 ORDER BY u.creation_date, u.user_id LIMIT 1

WITH act AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) n FROM (SELECT user_id FROM posts_questions UNION ALL SELECT user_id FROM posts_answers) GROUP BY user_id) SELECT u.display_name FROM users u JOIN act a USING (user_id) WHERE a.n = (SELECT min(n) FROM act) ORDER BY u.creation_date, u.user_id LIMIT 1
notes: Questions and answers only. Main: the oldest account with none, leaving out the Community system account. Also accepted: Community itself, and the oldest account with exactly one.

question: Across questions with the longest title length (150 characters), what is the average number of answers, comments and views?
reference_sql: SELECT AVG(answer_count) AS avg_answers, AVG((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c WHERE c.post_id = t.post_id)) AS avg_comments, AVG(view_count) AS avg_views FROM (SELECT post_id, answer_count, view_count FROM posts_questions WHERE length(title) = 150) t
alt_sqls: SELECT AVG(answer_count), AVG((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c WHERE c.post_id = t.post_id) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c JOIN posts_answers a ON a.post_id = c.post_id WHERE a.parent_id = t.post_id)), AVG(view_count) FROM (SELECT post_id, answer_count, view_count FROM posts_questions WHERE length(title) = 150) t
notes: 134 questions have a 150-character title. Main: comments directly on the question; also accepted: including comments on its answers.

question: Among users with at least 100 contributions (questions, answers and comments combined), which have the lowest reputation?
reference_sql: WITH act AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) n FROM (SELECT user_id FROM posts_questions UNION ALL SELECT user_id FROM posts_answers UNION ALL SELECT user_id FROM comments) GROUP BY user_id) SELECT u.display_name, u.reputation FROM users u JOIN act a USING (user_id) WHERE a.n >= 100 AND u.reputation = (SELECT min(u2.reputation) FROM users u2 JOIN act a2 USING (user_id) WHERE a2.n >= 100)
notes: All users tied at the lowest reputation (1) are listed.

question: Which users have the most activity for their reputation?
reference_sql: WITH act AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) n FROM (SELECT user_id FROM posts_questions UNION ALL SELECT user_id FROM posts_answers UNION ALL SELECT user_id FROM comments) GROUP BY user_id) SELECT u.display_name, 1.0 * a.n / u.reputation AS ratio FROM users u JOIN act a USING (user_id) ORDER BY ratio DESC, a.n DESC LIMIT 5
notes: Contributions per reputation point, top 5. Reputation 1 is common, so those accounts lead.

question: Excluding questions with fewer than 10 answers, which 5 questions generated the least activity?
reference_sql: SELECT q.title, q.answer_count + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c WHERE c.post_id = q.post_id) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c JOIN posts_answers a ON a.post_id = c.post_id WHERE a.parent_id = q.post_id) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM votes v WHERE v.post_id = q.post_id) AS activity FROM posts_questions q WHERE q.answer_count >= 10 ORDER BY activity, q.post_id LIMIT 5
alt_sqls: SELECT q.post_id, q.answer_count + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c WHERE c.post_id = q.post_id) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c JOIN posts_answers a ON a.post_id = c.post_id WHERE a.parent_id = q.post_id) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM votes v WHERE v.post_id = q.post_id) AS activity FROM posts_questions q WHERE q.answer_count >= 10 ORDER BY activity, q.post_id LIMIT 5
SELECT q.title, q.view_count FROM posts_questions q WHERE q.answer_count >= 10 ORDER BY q.view_count, q.post_id LIMIT 5
SELECT q.post_id, q.view_count FROM posts_questions q WHERE q.answer_count >= 10 ORDER BY q.view_count, q.post_id LIMIT 5
notes: 36 questions have 10 or more answers. Main: answers + comments + votes. Also accepted: ranking by views.

question: Which user answered the most questions in a single day?
reference_sql: SELECT u.display_name FROM posts_answers a JOIN users u ON u.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY a.user_id, date(a.creation_date) HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM posts_answers GROUP BY user_id, date(creation_date)))
notes: UTC calendar day. Gordon Linoff answered 8 questions on 2020-10-26; nobody else reached 8.

question: Who are the top 5 users by average answers per week?
reference_sql: SELECT u.display_name, COUNT(*) / 143.0 AS avg_per_week FROM posts_answers a JOIN users u ON u.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY a.user_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, u.display_name LIMIT 5
alt_sqls: SELECT u.display_name, COUNT(*) / ((julianday((SELECT MAX(creation_date) FROM posts_answers)) - julianday('2020-01-01')) / 7.0) AS avg_per_week FROM posts_answers a JOIN users u ON u.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY a.user_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, u.display_name LIMIT 5

SELECT u.display_name, COUNT(*) / ((julianday('2022-09-25') - julianday('2020-01-01')) / 7.0) AS avg_per_week FROM posts_answers a JOIN users u ON u.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY a.user_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, u.display_name LIMIT 5
notes: Answers divided by the 143 weeks in the data; the same ranking as total answers. The week count is a little different under other ways of counting weeks, so two close alternates are accepted.

question: Among users with at least 50 answers, who are the top 5 by average answers per active week?
reference_sql: SELECT u.display_name, 1.0 * COUNT(*) / COUNT(DISTINCT date(a.creation_date, 'weekday 0', '-6 days')) AS avg_per_active_week FROM posts_answers a JOIN users u ON u.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY a.user_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50 ORDER BY avg_per_active_week DESC, u.display_name LIMIT 5
alt_sqls: SELECT u.display_name, 1.0 * COUNT(*) / COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%W', a.creation_date)) AS avg_per_active_week FROM posts_answers a JOIN users u ON u.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY a.user_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50 ORDER BY avg_per_active_week DESC, u.display_name LIMIT 5

SELECT u.display_name, 1.0 * COUNT(*) / COUNT(DISTINCT date(a.creation_date, 'weekday 6', '-6 days')) AS avg_per_active_week FROM posts_answers a JOIN users u ON u.user_id = a.user_id GROUP BY a.user_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50 ORDER BY avg_per_active_week DESC, u.display_name LIMIT 5
notes: Averages differ slightly with where a week starts (Monday, Monday by year-week, Sunday); the top 5 and their order are the same.

question: For users with 25+ accepted answers, what is the average number of accepted answers?
reference_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) n FROM posts_answers WHERE is_accepted = 1 GROUP BY user_id HAVING n >= 25) SELECT AVG(n) FROM t
notes: 228 users have 25 or more accepted answers (counted by the answer flag); the average is about 59.4.

question: Which users in the western hemisphere answer the most at night?
notes: Users have no location (the users table holds only id, name, reputation, badges and account date).

question: Among users with 50+ accepted answers, how many have more than half of their answers posted between 10 PM and 5 AM US Eastern time (UTC-5, ignoring daylight saving)?
reference_sql: WITH acc AS (SELECT user_id FROM posts_answers WHERE is_accepted = 1 GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50), h AS (SELECT a.user_id, CAST(strftime('%H', datetime(a.creation_date, '-5 hours')) AS INT) hr FROM posts_answers a JOIN acc USING (user_id)) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT user_id, AVG(hr >= 22 OR hr < 5) f FROM h GROUP BY user_id HAVING f > 0.5)
notes: 73 users have 50 or more accepted answers. Night is 22:00-04:59 at a fixed UTC-5, more than half of all their answers.

question: Which question has the longest range from its first answer?
reference_sql: SELECT q.title FROM posts_answers a JOIN posts_questions q ON q.post_id = a.parent_id GROUP BY a.parent_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY julianday(MAX(a.creation_date)) - julianday(MIN(a.creation_date)) DESC LIMIT 1
alt_sqls: SELECT a.parent_id FROM posts_answers a GROUP BY a.parent_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY julianday(MAX(a.creation_date)) - julianday(MIN(a.creation_date)) DESC LIMIT 1
notes: Time between a question's first and last answer: question 59612976, about 986 days (next 971).

question: Which question waited the longest for its first answer?
reference_sql: SELECT q.title FROM posts_questions q JOIN posts_answers a ON a.parent_id = q.post_id GROUP BY q.post_id ORDER BY julianday(MIN(a.creation_date)) - julianday(q.creation_date) DESC LIMIT 1
alt_sqls: SELECT q.post_id FROM posts_questions q JOIN posts_answers a ON a.parent_id = q.post_id GROUP BY q.post_id ORDER BY julianday(MIN(a.creation_date)) - julianday(q.creation_date) DESC LIMIT 1
notes: Wait from the question to its first answer: question 59668208, about 953 days (next 942).

question: Second Life: How many questions received 100+ upvotes more than 3 days after they were posted?
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT q.post_id FROM votes v JOIN posts_questions q ON q.post_id = v.post_id WHERE v.vote_type = 'UpMod' AND julianday(v.creation_date) - julianday(q.creation_date) > 3 GROUP BY q.post_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100)
notes: Upvotes on the question itself, more than 3 days after it was posted (vote dates are whole days).

question: Second Life: How many questions received 100+ upvotes more than 7 days after they were posted?

notes: Same with 7 days. All 14 are also in the 3-day group.

question: How many answers with less than 12 characters have 10+ score?
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts_answers WHERE length(body) < 12 AND score >= 10

question: How many answers with less than 75 characters have a score of 10 or more?
reference_sql: WITH RECURSIVE s(id, t) AS (SELECT post_id, body FROM posts_answers WHERE score >= 10 UNION ALL SELECT id, substr(t, 1, instr(t, '<') - 1) || substr(t, instr(t, '<') + instr(substr(t, instr(t, '<')), '>')) FROM s WHERE instr(t, '<') > 0 AND instr(substr(t, instr(t, '<')), '>') > 0), f AS (SELECT id, t FROM s WHERE NOT (instr(t, '<') > 0 AND instr(substr(t, instr(t, '<')), '>') > 0)), g AS (SELECT id, trim(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(t, char(10), char(32)), char(13), char(32)), char(9), char(32)), char(160), char(32)), char(32) || char(32), char(32)), char(32) || char(32), char(32)), char(32) || char(32), char(32)), char(32) || char(32), char(32)), char(32) || char(32), char(32)), char(32) || char(32), char(32)), char(32) || char(32), char(32)), char(32) || char(32), char(32)), char(32) || char(32), char(32)), '<', '<'), '>', '>'), '"', '"'), ''', ''''), '&', '&')) AS vt FROM f) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM g WHERE length(vt) < 75
notes: Visible text only (tags removed, entities decoded, spaces collapsed), as the owner decided. Counting the stored HTML gives 3 and is NOT accepted.

reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE badge_count = 1

question: Tag twins: Which two tags appear together on the most questions?
reference_sql: SELECT t1.tag_name, t2.tag_name FROM post_tags a JOIN post_tags b ON a.post_id = b.post_id AND a.tag_id < b.tag_id JOIN tags t1 ON t1.tag_id = a.tag_id JOIN tags t2 ON t2.tag_id = b.tag_id GROUP BY a.tag_id, b.tag_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
notes: python and pandas appear together on 6,886 questions (next 6,494); either order.

question: Loners vs crowds: How many questions have just one tag, and how many have all five?
reference_sql: WITH n AS (SELECT post_id, COUNT(*) k FROM post_tags GROUP BY post_id) SELECT k, COUNT(*) FROM n WHERE k IN (1, 5) GROUP BY k
alt_sqls: WITH n AS (SELECT post_id, COUNT(*) k FROM post_tags GROUP BY post_id) SELECT SUM(k = 1), SUM(k = 5) FROM n
notes: 12,717 questions with one tag and 32,381 with five (five is the most any question has).

question: Rising vs falling: Which tag gained the most questions from 2020 to 2021, and which lost the most?
reference_sql: WITH y AS (SELECT t.tag_id, SUM(substr(q.creation_date, 1, 4) = '2020') c20, SUM(substr(q.creation_date, 1, 4) = '2021') c21 FROM post_tags t JOIN posts_questions q ON q.post_id = t.post_id GROUP BY t.tag_id) SELECT tag_name, c21 - c20 FROM y JOIN tags USING (tag_id) WHERE c21 - c20 = (SELECT MAX(c21 - c20) FROM y) UNION ALL SELECT tag_name, c21 - c20 FROM y JOIN tags USING (tag_id) WHERE c21 - c20 = (SELECT MIN(c21 - c20) FROM y)
alt_sqls: WITH y AS (SELECT t.tag_id, SUM(substr(q.creation_date, 1, 4) = '2020') c20, SUM(substr(q.creation_date, 1, 4) = '2021') c21 FROM post_tags t JOIN posts_questions q ON q.post_id = t.post_id GROUP BY t.tag_id) SELECT (SELECT tag_name FROM y JOIN tags USING (tag_id) ORDER BY c21 - c20 DESC LIMIT 1), (SELECT MAX(c21 - c20) FROM y), (SELECT tag_name FROM y JOIN tags USING (tag_id) ORDER BY c21 - c20 LIMIT 1), (SELECT MIN(c21 - c20) FROM y)
notes: Absolute change in questions per tag, 2020 to 2021: next.js +216 (next typescript +120), java -1,764 (next javascript -1,545).

question: Answered vs ignored: Among tags with at least 500 questions, which has the highest share of questions with an accepted answer, and which the lowest?
reference_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT t.tag_id, COUNT(*) n, AVG(q.accepted_answer_id IS NOT NULL) share FROM post_tags t JOIN posts_questions q ON q.post_id = t.post_id GROUP BY t.tag_id HAVING n >= 500) SELECT tag_name, share FROM s JOIN tags USING (tag_id) WHERE share = (SELECT MAX(share) FROM s) UNION ALL SELECT tag_name, share FROM s JOIN tags USING (tag_id) WHERE share = (SELECT MIN(share) FROM s)
alt_sqls: WITH s AS (SELECT t.tag_id, COUNT(*) n, AVG(q.accepted_answer_id IS NOT NULL) share FROM post_tags t JOIN posts_questions q ON q.post_id = t.post_id GROUP BY t.tag_id HAVING n >= 500) SELECT (SELECT tag_name FROM s JOIN tags USING (tag_id) ORDER BY share DESC LIMIT 1), (SELECT MAX(share) FROM s), (SELECT tag_name FROM s JOIN tags USING (tag_id) ORDER BY share LIMIT 1), (SELECT MIN(share) FROM s)
notes: 135 tags have 500 or more questions. Highest regex (61.0%), lowest npm (25.0%).

question: Night vs day: Do questions posted between 10 PM and 5 AM UTC get a higher average score than daytime ones?
reference_sql: SELECT AVG(score) FROM posts_questions GROUP BY (CAST(strftime('%H', creation_date) AS INT) >= 22 OR CAST(strftime('%H', creation_date) AS INT) < 5) ORDER BY (CAST(strftime('%H', creation_date) AS INT) >= 22 OR CAST(strftime('%H', creation_date) AS INT) < 5)

question: Accepted vs the rest: How much higher is the average score of accepted answers than other answers?

alt_sqls: SELECT (SELECT AVG(score) FROM posts_answers WHERE is_accepted = 1), (SELECT AVG(score) FROM posts_answers WHERE is_accepted = 0)
SELECT (SELECT AVG(score) FROM posts_answers WHERE is_accepted = 1) - (SELECT AVG(score) FROM posts_answers WHERE is_accepted = 0)
SELECT (SELECT AVG(score) FROM posts_answers WHERE is_accepted = 1) / (SELECT AVG(score) FROM posts_answers WHERE is_accepted = 0)
notes: Accepted answers average 1.526 against 0.668; the two averages, their difference (0.859) or their ratio (2.29) are accepted.

question: Veterans vs newcomers: Compare the average reputation and badge count of accounts older than 7 years (from the end of the data, 2022-09-25) with newer accounts.

notes: Accounts older than 7 years from the end of the data (created before 2015-09-25) against newer ones.

question: Year over year: By what percent did the number of questions change from 2020 to 2021, and from 2021 to 2022?
reference_sql: WITH y AS (SELECT CAST(substr(creation_date, 1, 4) AS INT) yr, COUNT(*) n FROM posts_questions GROUP BY 1) SELECT 100.0 * (b.n - a.n) / a.n FROM y a JOIN y b ON b.yr = a.yr + 1 ORDER BY a.yr
alt_sqls: WITH y AS (SELECT CAST(substr(creation_date, 1, 4) AS INT) yr, COUNT(*) n FROM posts_questions GROUP BY 1) SELECT (SELECT 100.0 * (b.n - a.n) / a.n FROM y a JOIN y b ON b.yr = a.yr + 1 WHERE a.yr = 2020), (SELECT 100.0 * (b.n - a.n) / a.n FROM y a JOIN y b ON b.yr = a.yr + 1 WHERE a.yr = 2021)
notes: -12.6% from 2020 to 2021 and -22.8% from 2021 to 2022; 2022 runs only to 25 September, so the second is a partial-year comparison.
